correctness.rationale: For all a>0,s>=0,H>0, N^2=0 gives the exact product [[D^-1,beta(t+2v)D^-2],[0,D^-1]] with v in [0,t^2/4]. The Euclidean operator norm has the stated closed form. The derivative of its logarithm has a sign-changing numerator strictly decreasing with v and hence admits no interior minima. The ratio of the two endpoint norms is strictly increasing with beta; its limits yield t_c=1+sqrt(5), and algebraic inversion yields beta_*(t). Strict inequality and tie conditions, endpoints and strictly positive infimum follow. verify.py independently checks identities with SymPy and 7272 direct SVD comparisons. No finite experiment is used as proof.

originality.rationale: A substantive comparison of claims and implication directions found no inspected theorem classifying terminal induced 2-norm of a product of exactly two variable-length ordinary backward-Euler resolvents on a damped Jordan shear. Reuter gives transient-growth criteria for exponentials and powers; Layton et al. treat a filtered DLN method; the published affine Jordan pencil result minimizes a differently constrained operator family. Own similar findings for normal oscillators are inapplicable to this defective nonnormal matrix. Exact titles/parameters are not used as novelty evidence; an unindexed or inaccessible historical equivalent remains a real priority risk.

value.rationale: The smallest nonnormal ODE test problem with a defective eigenvalue exhibits a structural optimization law distinct from scalar/normal eigenmode damping: exactly equal-or-sparse optimum and a horizon boundary at 1+sqrt(5). It supplies an exact fixed-budget prescription and shows that even a dissipative generator with s/a<2 can prefer omitting a second step. This is mathematically motivated by nonnormal transient-energy behavior and does not claim better physical-time accuracy or general matrix scope.
